newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP dealers bet on steady prices.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP dealers bet on steady prices.

text.p: BTP options dealers are trading on the assumption that the Italian bond market will remain stable and that options volatility will decline a little further in the next few days, traders said on Monday.
"People are more confident about range trades," said one trader from an Italian bank in London.
"They are selling straddles, and selling strangles."
BTP exchange-traded options were thinly traded on Monday, and took their lead from institutions trading in the over-the-counter market, dealers said.
BTP options volatility on LIFFE edged lower.
The Italian bank trader quoted at-the-money volatility at 7.2 to 7.3 percent at 1330 GMT, against Friday's close of 7.2 percent.
In the over-the-counter market, volatility on the three-month option exercisable into the 7.75 percent bond due 2006 was unchanged at 7.5 percent.
The derivatives markets are brushing off political and economic events in Italy, dealers said.
The Italian government called for a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Monday on budget measures introduced at the end of 1996.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi will hold a news conference at 1500 GMT on Monday to present revised statistics for 1992-1996, following Eurostat's approval on Friday of Italy's "Euro tax".
The currency is holding up well, inspiring confidence in Italy, but there will be no major slide in BTP options volatility from its current low level, dealers said.
"It is hard to see how we can have volatility substantially lower from here," said one dealer from a U.S. bank in London.
Concern that there will be a market squeeze on the bond which is cheapest to deliver into the LIFFE June BTP futures contract is also preventing a dramatic fall in options volatility, dealers said.
The 10.5 percent BTP due April 2005 was in short supply ahead of last week's expiry of the March BTP option, they added.
"People are wary of shorting the future," the Italian bank dealer said.
March BTP futures were trading at 131.15 at 1430 GMT, up 35 basis points. The June contract was 32 basis points higher at 130.50.
